I need to be careful here. The finding F004 is a settlement-to-document mismatch of 0.01 on invoice 165, not a closed-period posting issue. The fix convention says a correction may only void an invoice for duplicate_invoice findings, and other finding types must not change invoice status. So I must not change STAT_CD on invoice 165.

Also, the 0.01 difference between payments (1374.76) and invoice amount (1374.77) is a payment-side mismatch. Fixing it would require a journal or a new payment record, and the convention only supports correcting ledger amounts via a new journal. The journal 1270 itself balances (152.19 + 1222.58 = 1374.77 DR, equal to CR 1374.77), so there is no GL error to correct. Adjusting the GL to match a one-cent payment shortfall would invent an entry without a source document, and the payment record itself is the thing that would need to change, which I cannot do.

The correct action is to propose no correcting journal lines and no status changes, and explain why.

arguments.reasoning: No correction proposed. F004 is a settlement-to-document mismatch: invoice 165 (INV_AMT 1374.77, STAT_CD P) has payments totaling 1374.76, a 0.01 shortfall. This is not a closed-period posting, and the finding type does not authorize any invoice status change, so STAT_CD must stay P and no void (V) is applicable. The originating journal 1270 is internally consistent: DR 5100 152.19 + 5500 1222.58 = 1374.77, CR 2000 1374.77, posted in period 6 (closed, which is correct for a June invoice). Nothing in the GL is wrong for this invoice, so a one-cent adjusting journal would fabricate an entry to paper over a payment-side difference. The real discrepancy sits in APPAYM (the payment amount or a missing 0.01 payment record) and should be resolved by reviewing the source payment/remittance for invoice 165 before any ledger change. Note also that the 0.01 gap is the only paid-but-mismatched invoice in the data.
